newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares break records in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares break records in early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares broke bourse records in early floor trade on Friday, having traded in a tight range at record levels in electronic trade earlier on.
A combination of factors prompted the more bullish mood in Frankfurt, notably the stronger dollar, firmer Bunds and the 0.30 percent higher overnight close on Wall Street.

In early bourse the DAX index, which monitors trade in 30 blue-chip German stocks, was up 20.02 points, or 0.78 percent, at 2,590.34 points. The DAX hit a bourse all-time high of 2,592.65 points earlier on.
Traders said U.S. consumer prices and retail sales data due at 1230 GMT could have a big impact on trade, as the market is watching closely for signs of inflationary pressure there.
Some traders said further gains could be limited. "I don't think there is enough impetus to break out of the current ranges just yet," said one trader.
Others said the continued strength of the dollar could be enough to push the DAX index over the psychologically-important 2,600 point threshold.
Chemical stocks led the market in terms of number of shares traded, but they registered mixed performances.
BASF AG was up 53 pfennigs at 45.60 marks and Bayer AG was up 48 pfennigs at 54.75 marks, but Hoechst AG was down 49 pfennigs at 53.45 marks, amid some profit-taking.
Deutsche Bank AG continued its rally of recent days after Thursday's confirmation that UBS investment bank had upgraded Deutsche, with its shares up 60 pfennigs at 72.20 marks.
